summary.title: Dapagliflozin at a glance
points: An SGLT2 inhibitor: sugar, salt and water leave in the urine. One 10 mg tablet a day.
Three EU uses: type 2 diabetes (from age 10), symptomatic chronic heart failure, chronic kidney disease. Only the first needs diabetes.
HbA1c about −0.5 to −0.7 points added to other medicines; matched glipizide with far less hypoglycaemia.
Outcomes: DAPA-HF HR 0.74, DELIVER 0.82, DAPA-CKD 9.2% vs 14.5%; DECLARE neutral on heart attack and stroke.
Watch genital infections, volume depletion, ketoacidosis (even at near-normal sugar), Fournier's gangrene.

exercises.scenario: A cardiologist wants to start Forxiga in a 68-year-old with heart failure who doesn't have diabetes.

questions.prompt: Does the indication allow it?
options: Only if HbA1c is above 6.5% at the start of treatment
No: every Forxiga indication requires type 2 diabetes first
Only at 5 mg, since the 10 mg dose is for diabetes
Yes: the heart-failure use doesn't need diabetes
questions.explanation: Heart failure and chronic kidney disease are indications in their own right.

questions.prompt: Which side effect is most frequent overall?
options: Hypoglycaemia when taken on its own
Diabetic ketoacidosis at near-normal sugar
Genital infections
Fournier's gangrene of the genital area
questions.explanation: 5.5% vs 0.6% on placebo; mostly mild and treatable.

exercises.scenario: A partner deck says 'dapagliflozin prevents heart attacks in diabetes'.

questions.prompt: What did DECLARE show?
options: A significant 7% reduction in heart attacks and strokes
Non-inferior, but no reduction in heart attack, stroke or CV death
A benefit only in people with established disease
A rise in heart attacks offset by fewer strokes
questions.explanation: HR 0.93 (95% CI 0.84–1.03). Its clear effect was on heart-failure hospitalisation.

questions.prompt: How was DAPA-CKD's result expressed in absolute terms?
options: 5.3 percentage points lower
14.5% lower, the placebo rate itself
4 fewer events per 100 patient-years
39 percentage points lower over the trial
questions.explanation: 9.2% vs 14.5%: 39% relative, 5.3 points absolute.

summary.title: How it works
points: Blocks SGLT2 in the proximal tubule: about 70 g of sugar a day leaves in the urine at 10 mg.
Highly selective over SGLT1 and insulin-independent, so little hypoglycaemia on its own.
Salt and osmotic diuresis lower pressure inside the kidney's filters via tubuloglomerular feedback.
Glucose effect fades as GFR falls; heart and kidney effects work through salt, water and pressure.
Cleared by UGT1A9, half-life about 13 hours; few level interactions, but watch diuretics, lithium, insulin and sulphonylureas.

exercises.scenario: A patient's GFR falls from 70 to 35 while on dapagliflozin for diabetes and kidney disease.

questions.prompt: What happens to the glucose effect?
options: It gets stronger because exposure rises by over a half
It disappears, so the drug should be stopped at once
Nothing changes, because the dose is fixed at 10 mg
It weakens, while the kidney benefit persists
questions.explanation: Sugar removal depends on filtration; organ protection works through salt, water and pressure.

questions.prompt: Should the dose change?
options: Yes: switch to the combination tablet with metformin
No: 10 mg regardless of kidney function
Yes: halve it to 5 mg below GFR 45 to limit exposure
Yes: double it to 20 mg to restore the glucose effect
questions.explanation: Exposure rises a little, but the dose doesn't change.

exercises.scenario: A colleague asks why dapagliflozin protects the kidney even though it removes less sugar there.

questions.prompt: What's the mechanism proposed in the SmPC?
options: More salt downstream lowers pressure inside the filters
More sugar in the urine washes toxins out of the kidney
It increases insulin release, which protects the tubules
It blocks SGLT1 in the gut, cutting the kidney's workload
questions.explanation: Tubuloglomerular feedback narrows the vessel feeding each filter.

questions.prompt: Why does haematocrit rise by about 2.3 points?
options: It signals a bleeding risk that needs urgent investigation
It's a lab error caused by sugar in the sample tube
The blood holds less water
The bone marrow makes more red cells under SGLT2 blockade
questions.explanation: A marker of fluid shift; a marked rise above 55% should still be investigated.

summary.title: History
points: Developed by BMS and AstraZeneca; centralised EU licence in November 2012 for type 2 diabetes.
Class-wide Article 20 reviews: ketoacidosis (2016) and amputations (2017).
Type 1 diabetes (5 mg, BMI ≥27) approved in 2019; withdrawn by the company in 2021, with no new safety concern.
DAPA-HF, DAPA-CKD and DELIVER added heart failure and kidney disease (2020–2022), without needing diabetes.
Children from age 10 added for type 2 diabetes.

exercises.scenario: A pharmacist asks why a patient's type 1 diabetes prescription for Forxiga 5 mg was stopped in 2021.

questions.prompt: What's accurate?
options: The company withdrew the indication; there was no new safety concern
The EMA withdrew it after a new safety signal in type 1 patients
The FDA's 2019 refusal forced the EU to remove it
It never had an EU licence, only off-label use
questions.explanation: Ketoacidosis had been common in the type 1 trials; possible confusion with wide use was cited.

questions.prompt: What happened to the extra safety materials?
options: They became a condition of the kidney indication
They moved into the type 2 diabetes PIL unchanged
They were extended to every heart-failure patient
They were discontinued
questions.explanation: Additional risk minimisation measures ended with the indication.

exercises.scenario: How did a diabetes drug become a heart-failure and kidney drug?

questions.prompt: What drove the change?
options: The 2017 amputation review, which widened its use
Large outcome trials (DAPA-HF, DAPA-CKD, DELIVER)
Generic competition that forced a new positioning
A new formulation that targets the heart directly
questions.explanation: Variations assessed 2020–2022 added the indications.

questions.prompt: What is an Article 20 referral?
options: An arbitration between member states in mutual recognition
A national review of generics before they launch
The EU safety review for centrally authorised medicines
A company's voluntary withdrawal of an indication
questions.explanation: SGLT2 inhibitors had two: ketoacidosis and amputations.

summary.title: What it's approved for
points: Type 2 diabetes from age 10, as an adjunct; monotherapy only if metformin isn't tolerated.
The partner list is open: 'in addition to other medicinal products for type 2 diabetes'.
Heart failure: symptomatic chronic, no ejection-fraction limit (DAPA-HF ≤40%, DELIVER >40%).
Chronic kidney disease: broad wording, but no experience without diabetes and without albuminuria.
Not covered: type 1 diabetes; children with heart failure or kidney disease.

exercises.scenario: A 60-year-old without diabetes has chronic kidney disease, eGFR 50, no albuminuria.

questions.prompt: What does the SmPC say?
options: Allowed only at 5 mg until albuminuria appears
Covered by the wording, but without trial experience
Contraindicated, because albuminuria is a condition of the licence
Not covered, because the kidney use needs diabetes
questions.explanation: DAPA-CKD enrolled people with albuminuria; patients with albuminuria may benefit more.

questions.prompt: A patient with type 2 diabetes has a contraindication to metformin but tolerates it. Can Forxiga be used alone?
options: Yes: monotherapy covers contraindications and intolerance
Yes, but only in children aged 10 to 17
Not under the wording: monotherapy needs intolerance
No: Forxiga can never be used alone in diabetes
questions.explanation: Januvia's wording covers both; Forxiga's says 'due to intolerance'.

exercises.scenario: A heart-failure nurse asks whether ejection fraction matters for prescribing.

questions.prompt: What does the indication say?
options: Only 40% or below, as in DAPA-HF
Only above 40%, as in DELIVER
Only between 41% and 49%
No ejection-fraction limit
questions.explanation: The two trials together cover the range.

questions.prompt: Which group has limited experience?
options: NYHA class IV
Patients with ejection fraction above 60%
Patients without diabetes
Patients over 75 with NYHA class II
questions.explanation: Infiltrative cardiomyopathy wasn't studied either.

summary.title: Strengths and products
points: Forxiga 5 mg (round, 1427) and 10 mg (diamond, 1428); yellow, contain lactose; calendar blisters.
MAH AstraZeneca AB (Södertälje); one SmPC for the whole EU.
Duplicates: Edistride (with Forxiga), Ebymect (with Xigduo).
Xigduo: 5 mg + metformin, twice daily with a meal. Qtern: with saxagliptin.
Generics authorised centrally on bioequivalence.

exercises.scenario: A heart-failure patient is offered Xigduo to 'simplify tablets'.

questions.prompt: What's the problem?
options: Xigduo is a generic without a heart-failure licence yet
Xigduo is licensed for type 2 diabetes only
Nothing; all dapagliflozin products share the same uses
Xigduo contains saxagliptin, which is barred in heart failure
questions.explanation: Only Forxiga carries the heart-failure and kidney indications.

questions.prompt: How is Xigduo taken?
options: Once a day at any time, like Forxiga
Three times a day before each main meal
Once a week, as a prolonged-release tablet
Twice a day with a meal
questions.explanation: Each tablet holds 5 mg dapagliflozin plus metformin.

exercises.scenario: A BD colleague sees 'Edistride' and 'Ebymect' in an EMA list.

questions.prompt: What are they?
options: Duplicate licences of Forxiga and Xigduo
New molecules in the same class
Products withdrawn after the 2017 review
Generic copies made by other companies
questions.explanation: A second licence for the same product under another name.

questions.prompt: Which dapagliflozin product pairs it with a DPP-4 inhibitor?
options: Ebymect, the Xigduo duplicate
Edistride, the Forxiga duplicate
Qtern
Xigduo, with metformin
questions.explanation: Saxagliptin plus dapagliflozin.

summary.title: How it's taken
points: 10 mg once daily for all indications, any time, with or without food.
Missed dose: 12 hours or more to the next dose, take it; less, skip it. Never double.
No dose change for kidney function; don't start below GFR 25; expect an early eGFR dip.
Severe liver impairment: start at 5 mg.
Sick-day rule: pause for major surgery, serious illness or fluid loss; check ketones before restarting.

exercises.scenario: A patient on dapagliflozin has gastroenteritis with vomiting and can't drink.

questions.prompt: What does the SmPC recommend?
options: Switch to 5 mg for the duration of the illness
Continue, but double the water intake to compensate
Continue as normal; vomiting doesn't affect it
Pause until the fluid loss is corrected
questions.explanation: Watch for ketoacidosis, which can occur at near-normal sugar.

questions.prompt: She forgot this morning's dose and the next one is in 8 hours.
options: Take two tablets tomorrow morning
Skip it
Take it now, and the next one as usual
Take half a tablet now and half later
questions.explanation: Less than 12 hours to the next dose: skip.

exercises.scenario: A patient with GFR 22 asks to start dapagliflozin for kidney disease.

questions.prompt: What does the SmPC say?
options: Starting isn't recommended below GFR 25
It's formally contraindicated below GFR 30
Start at 5 mg and increase if tolerated
Start at 10 mg; the dose never changes
questions.explanation: Patients already on treatment may continue, as in DAPA-CKD.

questions.prompt: Two weeks after starting, eGFR falls by 4 points. What's this?
options: Proof the drug isn't working for this patient
A lab error caused by sugar in the urine
The expected early dip
A sign of kidney injury that requires stopping
questions.explanation: In DAPA-CKD, the long-term decline was slower on dapagliflozin.

summary.title: Reading a clinical trial
points: Hierarchical testing: once a step fails, later results are only nominal.
Check which component drives a composite (DECLARE: hospitalisations, not deaths).
Rate ratios count first and repeat events; win ratios score patient-reported symptoms.
Trials stopped early may overstate the size of the effect.
Pooled analyses can show what single trials couldn't (DAPA-HF + DELIVER: CV death HR 0.85).

exercises.scenario: DECLARE reports a renal composite HR of 0.76.

questions.prompt: Why isn't this a confirmed benefit?
options: Kidney outcomes weren't measured in DECLARE at all
The confidence interval crosses 1.0 for the kidney outcome
The trial was stopped early for the kidney result
Hierarchical testing had already stopped
questions.explanation: Superiority on heart attack, stroke or CV death wasn't shown (p = 0.172), so later tests are nominal.

questions.prompt: DECLARE's HF-or-death composite was HR 0.83. What drove it?
options: Fewer cardiovascular deaths, with hospitalisations unchanged
Fewer heart attacks counted inside the composite
Fewer heart-failure hospitalisations
An equal share of deaths and hospitalisations
questions.explanation: Hospitalisation HR 0.73; CV death HR 0.98.

exercises.scenario: DAPA-HF reports a rate ratio of 0.75 and a KCCQ win ratio of 1.18.

questions.prompt: What does the rate ratio add?
options: The benefit holds for repeat events, not just first ones
It shows symptoms improved, measured by patients
It replaces the hazard ratio as the primary result
It shows the drug works faster than the hazard ratio suggests
questions.explanation: All events counted: 567 vs 742.

questions.prompt: What does a win ratio above 1 mean?
options: Patients on placebo did better more often
Patients on the drug did better more often
The trial met its non-inferiority margin
The drug lowered HbA1c more than placebo
questions.explanation: Each drug patient is compared with each placebo patient.

summary.title: The pivotal trials
points: DECLARE (diabetes): heart attack/stroke/CV death non-inferior, not superior; HF hospitalisation or CV death HR 0.83.
DAPA-HF (EF ≤40%): HR 0.74 on top of full heart-failure treatment, with or without diabetes.
DELIVER (EF >40%): HR 0.82; smaller effect, older patients.
DAPA-CKD: 9.2% vs 14.5%, with or without diabetes; stopped early; also fewer deaths.
vs glipizide: equal HbA1c, weight −3.2 vs +1.4 kg, hypoglycaemia 3.5% vs 40.8%.

exercises.scenario: A payer asks whether dapagliflozin should be preferred to cut heart attacks in diabetes.

questions.prompt: What's the evidence-based answer?
options: Only in people with prior heart attacks
Yes: DECLARE showed a significant 7% reduction
Yes: DAPA-HF showed fewer heart attacks
No: DECLARE showed no reduction
questions.explanation: Its clear effects are on heart failure and the kidneys.

questions.prompt: Why does the EU heart-failure indication have no ejection-fraction limit?
options: DAPA-HF and DELIVER together cover the range
DAPA-HF included preserved ejection fraction too
The EMA extrapolated from DECLARE's heart-failure data
DELIVER alone covered every ejection fraction

exercises.scenario: Compare the glipizide trial's 52-week and 208-week results.

questions.prompt: Why treat the 208-week figures with caution?
options: HbA1c was measured with a different method
Fewer than 40% of patients remained
The trial switched to a placebo comparator
The glipizide dose was raised after 52 weeks
questions.explanation: Long-term figures rest on a shrinking group.

questions.prompt: What makes DAPA-CKD's size of effect uncertain?
options: It measured only albuminuria
It enrolled only people with diabetes
It was stopped early for efficacy
It had no placebo arm
questions.explanation: Direction reliable; size possibly overstated.

summary.title: Combination trials
points: Forxiga's partner list is open; licensed single tablets exist only with metformin (Xigduo) and saxagliptin (Qtern).
No combination licence with a statin, GLP-1 RA or blood-pressure medicine: those are co-administered.
DURATION-8: with exenatide, −1.98 vs −1.39 and −1.60 points, plus lower weight and BP.
Key interaction lines: diuretics add up; insulin and sulphonylureas need lower doses; simvastatin change not relevant.
Statin and GLP-1 RA columns have no outcome data; the BP column does (DAPA-CKD).

exercises.scenario: A partner proposes a dapagliflozin + semaglutide single tablet for the EU.

questions.prompt: What evidence exists for the pairing?
options: A dedicated SmPC interaction line
A large outcome trial with semaglutide
An EU licence for a similar combination
Only exenatide data (DURATION-8), glucose and weight
questions.explanation: Exenatide is one GLP-1 RA; others weren't studied here.

questions.prompt: Which combination does have licensed EU single tablets?
options: With an ACE inhibitor, for kidney disease
With exenatide, as a weekly product
With metformin, and with saxagliptin
With a statin, for cardiovascular risk
questions.explanation: Xigduo/Ebymect and Qtern.

exercises.scenario: A patient on a loop diuretic starts dapagliflozin.

questions.prompt: What's the main concern?
options: Lower dapagliflozin levels through UGT1A9 induction
Dehydration and low blood pressure
Hypoglycaemia through added insulin release
Higher diuretic blood levels through CYP inhibition
questions.explanation: The water-losing effects add up.

questions.prompt: Why can't you rank the six combination columns?
options: Different trials and starting HbA1c
They all started at the same HbA1c
Only the statin column used placebo
They were compared head-to-head in DECLARE
questions.explanation: The biggest falls came from trials starting above 9%.

summary.title: Heart-attack and stroke outcomes
points: Heart attacks and strokes: no reduction in DECLARE (HR 0.93).
Heart failure: fewer hospitalisations in DECLARE (0.73), DAPA-HF (0.74) and DELIVER (0.82).
Kidneys: slower decline in DAPA-CKD; DECLARE's kidney result is nominal.
Death: lower in DAPA-CKD; pooled heart-failure trials CV death HR 0.85.
The benefits act on fluid, pressure and kidneys, not on plaque.

exercises.scenario: Which outcome did dapagliflozin NOT improve?

questions.prompt: Choose one.
options: Heart attack, stroke and CV death in type 2 diabetes
Hospitalisation for heart failure in DECLARE
The heart-failure composite above 40% ejection fraction
Decline in kidney function in DAPA-CKD
questions.explanation: DECLARE: HR 0.93, not superior.

questions.prompt: What did pooling DAPA-HF and DELIVER show?
options: Higher death in preserved ejection fraction
Fewer strokes than either trial alone
No difference in any outcome at all
Lower CV death (HR 0.85)
questions.explanation: Neither trial showed it clearly on its own.

exercises.scenario: A colleague asks why dapagliflozin helps the heart but not heart attacks.

questions.prompt: What's the best explanation?
options: It lowers LDL cholesterol only modestly
It acts on fluid, pressure and kidneys, not plaque
It raises blood pressure in some patients
It was tested only in people without heart disease
questions.explanation: Lesson 14 shows how guidelines use this.

questions.prompt: How should DECLARE's heart-attack HR of 0.89 be read?
options: A signal of harm
A confirmed 11% reduction
Nominal; no claim of fewer heart attacks
The primary result of the trial
questions.explanation: Component results after the hierarchy stopped.

summary.title: Side effects
points: Genital infections 5.5% vs 0.6% (women 8.4% vs 1.2%); mostly mild; phimosis reported.
Ketoacidosis can be euglycaemic (sugar below 14 mmol/L); don't restart without a resolved trigger.
Fournier's gangrene: very rare, urgent surgery and antibiotics.
Fluid loss and an early creatinine rise, mostly small and reversible.
Hypoglycaemia mainly with sulphonylureas or insulin; amputation is an open class question.

exercises.scenario: A patient on dapagliflozin has nausea, abdominal pain and fast breathing. Glucose is 11 mmol/L.

questions.prompt: What should happen?
options: Assess for ketoacidosis now; stop if suspected
Double the insulin dose and recheck tomorrow
Continue and recheck symptoms next week
Reassure: glucose isn't high enough for ketoacidosis
questions.explanation: Euglycaemic ketoacidosis is easy to miss.

questions.prompt: After an episode with no clear trigger, can she restart?
options: Yes, if she also takes insulin
Yes, at the 5 mg dose
Not recommended
Yes, after one week off treatment
questions.explanation: Restart only if a clear trigger was found and resolved.

exercises.scenario: A man reports genital pain, redness and fever.

questions.prompt: What must be ruled out?
options: A urinary infection treated at home
An ordinary genital yeast infection only
Phimosis needing elective circumcision
Fournier's gangrene
questions.explanation: Rare but life-threatening; urgent treatment.

questions.prompt: A patient on glimepiride has repeated hypos after starting dapagliflozin.
options: Stop dapagliflozin permanently
Consider lowering the sulphonylurea dose
Increase dapagliflozin to 20 mg
Hypoglycaemia can't be linked to it
questions.explanation: 6.0% vs 2.1% with glimepiride.

summary.title: Who shouldn't take it, and interactions
points: Only contraindication: allergy.
'Should not be used': type 1 diabetes, breastfeeding. 'Not recommended': 2nd–3rd trimester, starting below GFR 25.
Extra care: fluid-loss risk, ketoacidosis risk factors, NYHA IV.
Effect interactions: diuretics, insulin/sulphonylureas, lithium (levels fall).
Xigduo inherits metformin's rules, including heart-failure restrictions.

exercises.scenario: A patient on lithium is starting dapagliflozin.

questions.prompt: What does the SmPC advise?
options: Nothing; dapagliflozin doesn't affect lithium
Halve the dapagliflozin dose
Stop lithium while on dapagliflozin
Monitor lithium more often; involve its prescriber
questions.explanation: Dapagliflozin can lower lithium levels.

questions.prompt: Which is a formal contraindication?
options: Type 1 diabetes
Allergy to dapagliflozin or an ingredient
Breastfeeding
GFR below 25
questions.explanation: The others are 'should not be used' or 'not recommended'.

exercises.scenario: A heart-failure patient with diabetes is moved from Forxiga + metformin to Xigduo.

questions.prompt: What's the irony?
options: Xigduo carries metformin's heart-failure restrictions
Nothing; the rules are identical
Xigduo has a broader heart-failure licence than Forxiga
Xigduo removes the need for kidney monitoring
questions.explanation: Combining two medicines combines both sets of rules.

questions.prompt: Who has a higher ketoacidosis risk?
options: Someone on metformin alone
Someone with high C-peptide
Someone whose insulin dose was just cut
Someone with NYHA class II
questions.explanation: Low insulin reserve, illness, alcohol and dehydration also raise it.

summary.title: Pharmacovigilance
points: 2016 class review: atypical ketoacidosis; stop if suspected, pause for surgery, care with risk factors.
2017 amputation review (from canagliflozin's CANVAS): no increase with dapagliflozin, but a class warning on foot care.
DAPA-CKD doubled as the post-authorisation safety study for amputation.
2021 DHPC ended the type 1 indication without a new safety concern.
Watch: amputation as a class question, and ketoacidosis around surgery.

exercises.scenario: A partner asks why the Forxiga label warns about amputations if DECLARE showed no increase.

questions.prompt: What's the explanation?
options: DECLARE showed more amputations with dapagliflozin
A class review couldn't exclude a class effect
Amputation is a common side effect in the SmPC
The FDA required the warning for the EU too
questions.explanation: Triggered by canagliflozin; data for dapagliflozin were limited.

questions.prompt: Which study tracked the amputation risk after approval?
options: DAPA-CKD, as a PASS
DELIVER, as a sub-study
DECLARE, as the primary outcome
A separate registry in type 1 diabetes
questions.explanation: The kidney trial doubled as a post-authorisation safety study.

exercises.scenario: Most of dapagliflozin's safety decisions weren't specific to it.

questions.prompt: Why?
options: Dapagliflozin has never had a safety review
They came from US labels
The EU only reviews generics
They were class reviews of all SGLT2 inhibitors
questions.explanation: Ketoacidosis (2016) and amputations (2017).

questions.prompt: What should trigger a module refresh?
options: A new US brand name
A new generic launch
A PRAC signal on SGLT2 inhibitors
A competitor price cut
questions.explanation: Also new product information or a PSUSA with a label change.

summary.title: ESC guidelines
points: HFrEF: one of four pillars with an ACEi/ARB/ARNI, beta-blocker and MRA.
2023 update: dapagliflozin or empagliflozin Class I A in HFmrEF and HFpEF.
Type 2 diabetes + CKD: Class I A to reduce HF hospitalisation or CV death.
Diabetes with ASCVD: SGLT2 inhibitor and/or GLP-1 RA, whatever the sugar.
Label and guidelines align closely; gap: CKD without diabetes or albuminuria.

exercises.scenario: A patient with HFpEF (EF 58%) and diabetes asks what's evidence-based.

questions.prompt: Which drug class is Class I there?
options: None; it's all Class IIb
ACE inhibitors only
SGLT2 inhibitors (plus diuretics for fluid)
Beta-blockers and MRAs
questions.explanation: Other pillars remain IIb above 40%.

questions.prompt: Which trial supports this?
options: DECLARE
DAPA-HF
DURATION-8
DELIVER
questions.explanation: With empagliflozin's EMPEROR-Preserved.

exercises.scenario: Compare this module's label–guideline fit with sitagliptin's.

questions.prompt: What's different?
options: Sitagliptin is Class I for heart failure
Here they align; sitagliptin's label lagged practice
Both labels lag practice equally
Dapagliflozin's guideline is weaker
questions.explanation: Both drop the ejection-fraction split for SGLT2 inhibitors.

questions.prompt: Where's the remaining gap?
options: CKD without diabetes and without albuminuria
Type 2 diabetes in adults
Heart failure above 60% ejection fraction
Use with metformin
questions.explanation: No trial experience in that group.

summary.title: The medicine and its story
points: A kidney-acting drug whose sugar effect needs filtration, but whose organ benefits don't.
Three indications today; type 1 came and went (2019–2021).
Class reviews (2016–2017) shaped today's warnings.
Outcome trials turned a diabetes drug into a heart and kidney drug.

exercises.scenario: A new BD colleague asks why dapagliflozin's market is bigger than its diabetes use.

questions.prompt: What's the core reason?
options: It regained a type 1 diabetes licence in 2023
Heart-failure and kidney uses don't need diabetes
It became first-line in type 2 diabetes in 2020
It's licensed for weight loss in obesity
questions.explanation: DAPA-HF, DAPA-CKD and DELIVER added indications for anyone with these conditions.

questions.prompt: Why do its heart and kidney effects persist when GFR falls?
options: Insulin release increases as GFR falls
The dose is doubled in kidney impairment
They work through salt, water and pressure
Exposure falls, which protects the kidney
questions.explanation: Only the sugar effect depends on filtration.

questions.prompt: What was cited for withdrawing type 1 use?
options: An FDA order
Lack of any HbA1c benefit
A new signal of liver injury
Possible confusion amid wide use; DKA was common in trials
questions.explanation: No new safety concern.

exercises.scenario: Link mechanism to safety.

questions.prompt: Why can ketoacidosis occur with near-normal sugar?
options: Sugar is lost in urine, masking the usual high glucose
The drug blocks ketone excretion
Insulin levels rise sharply
It stimulates glucagon only at night
questions.explanation: So check ketones whatever the glucose.

questions.prompt: Why is hypoglycaemia rare on its own?
options: It's taken with food
Sugar removal falls as blood sugar normalises
It blocks SGLT1 in the gut
It releases glucagon continuously
questions.explanation: Insulin-independent and glucose-dependent removal.

questions.prompt: In your own words: why does the label keep the 10 mg dose when kidney function falls, but warn the sugar effect fades?
questions.modelAnswer: Exposure only rises modestly in kidney impairment, so no dose change is needed for safety. But the sugar removed depends on how much the kidneys filter, so glucose lowering fades below GFR 45, while the heart and kidney benefits continue through salt, water and pressure effects.

summary.title: The label in practice
points: Indications: diabetes (monotherapy only if metformin isn't tolerated), heart failure at any EF, CKD.
Products: Forxiga for all uses; Xigduo and Qtern for diabetes only.
10 mg daily; no kidney dose change; don't start below GFR 25; 5 mg start in severe liver impairment.
Sick-day rule and the 12-hour missed-dose rule.

exercises.scenario: A 74-year-old with HFrEF and CKD (GFR 28), no diabetes, on a loop diuretic.

questions.prompt: Can dapagliflozin be started?
options: No: heart failure without diabetes isn't covered
Yes, but at 5 mg because of age
Yes: 10 mg, GFR is above 25
No: GFR must be above 45 to start
questions.explanation: Both heart failure and CKD indications apply.

questions.prompt: What extra care applies?
options: Fluid loss with the diuretic
Hypoglycaemia from the diuretic
Higher lithium levels
Lactose content of Xigduo
questions.explanation: Older age and diuretics raise the risk.

questions.prompt: He's admitted for surgery. What's the rule?
options: Switch to Xigduo in hospital
Continue throughout surgery
Double the dose after surgery
Pause; restart when ketones are normal and he's stable
questions.explanation: Sick-day rule.

exercises.scenario: A diabetes patient on Forxiga + metformin wants one tablet.

questions.prompt: Which product and schedule?
options: Edistride, twice daily

summary.title: The evidence
points: Read hierarchy, components, repeat events and early stopping before trusting a number.
Neutral on heart attack and stroke; consistent on heart failure and kidneys.
Combinations: licensed with metformin and saxagliptin; GLP-1 RA and statin columns lack outcomes.
Death benefit: DAPA-CKD, and pooled heart-failure trials.

questions.prompt: In your own words: what does it mean that DECLARE's kidney results are 'nominal'?
questions.modelAnswer: The trial tested its endpoints in a fixed order. Because superiority on heart attack, stroke or CV death wasn't shown, testing formally stopped, so later results like the kidney composite are calculated but not protected against chance. They're supportive, not confirmed.

summary.title: Safety and guidelines
points: Genital infections, euglycaemic ketoacidosis, Fournier's gangrene, fluid loss, early eGFR dip.
Only contraindication is allergy; type 1 diabetes and breastfeeding should not be used.
Class reviews: ketoacidosis 2016, amputations 2017; DAPA-CKD as PASS.
ESC: one of four pillars in HFrEF; Class I A above 40% EF and in diabetes with CKD.

summary.title: Dapagliflozin: the whole picture
points: An SGLT2 inhibitor whose organ benefits don't depend on blood sugar.
Diabetes, heart failure at any EF, and CKD; type 1 withdrawn in 2021.
Neutral on heart attacks; consistent on heart failure, kidneys and some deaths.
10 mg for all uses; don't start below GFR 25; sick-day pauses.
Safety: genital infections, euglycaemic ketoacidosis, Fournier's, fluid loss; class reviews.
Guidelines: a pillar of heart-failure care, aligned with the label.
